memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He said to the Israelites, "In the future when your descendants ask their parents, 'What do these stones mean?' tell them, 'Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.'" — Josh 4:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua returns to the theme of the children's question, and now he gives the exact answer parents are to speak: "Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground." Simple, clear, true. When the little ones ask about the stones, the story to tell is not about how clever or strong Israel was. It is about what God did — He made a way through the impossible.

This is how faith is to be handed down: honestly, plainly, giving God the glory. Joshua does not tell the parents to weave an elaborate tale or to boast of Israel's greatness. He tells them to state the simple fact of God's deliverance. The best testimony is often the plainest one: "This is what God did for us."

Notice how central the next generation is to God's heart. Twice in this chapter God brings up the children's future question. He is deeply concerned that faith not die with one generation but be passed faithfully to the next. Our children and grandchildren need to hear the story from us.

The gospel itself is meant to be handed on this way, from those who have received it to those who come after (2 Tim 2:2). We tell the young what God has done, supremely in sending His Son to make a way for us to cross from death to life. Let us be faithful storytellers of grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When younger ones ask about your faith, do you point them to what God has done?
2. Are you telling the "story" simply and giving God the glory, rather than boasting of yourself?
3. Who in the next generation is God calling you to pass faith along to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me tell the next generation plainly what You have done. Let the story of Your grace, fulfilled in Christ, pass faithfully to those who come after me. Amen.
